title: sip two C nine and warfarin

segs.text: Section eleven. sip two C nine. Two C nine, cytochrome P four fifty, family two C nine, is a liver enzyme that metabolizes, and so clears, several narrow therapeutic index drugs, where a small change in clearance changes the outcome: warfarin, phenytoin, glipizide and tolbutamide.

Two common variants, star two and star three, make a low activity enzyme. Compared with the normal star one enzyme, the star two enzyme keeps about twenty percent of the activity, and the star three enzyme about five percent, so star three is the more severe loss. The C P I C warfarin guideline gives different figures: S warfarin metabolism drops about thirty to forty percent with star two and eighty to ninety percent with star three.

Why a lower dose? Two C nine clears warfarin. A low activity variant clears it slowly, the drug builds up, and with a narrow therapeutic index the patient moves into the bleeding range unless the starting dose is lowered. These variants lower the dose, never raise it.

Two studies agree. Warfarin is a mixture of two mirror image forms, R and S, and S is the more potent. The first study measured clearance: two copies of star three cleared S warfarin about ninety percent less than two copies of star one. The second started from the patients who need the lowest dose: the usual start is about five milligrams a day, these patients need about one point five milligrams. At least eighty percent of them carry these low activity variants.

Frequency differs by population. About thirty percent of Caucasians carry star two or star three, the highest. About one to three percent of African Americans do, but in African ancestry other low activity variants, star five, six, eight and eleven, are together more common. In the East Asians studied, almost none carried them, and the C P I C guideline says star two is virtually absent in Asians.

Many drugs also inhibit two C nine. An inhibitor and a low activity variant both lower the enzyme's activity, and the two add up rather than cancel, so a drug the enzyme clears can reach concentrations that are too high.
